page.text:
The distinction between Separation and Replacement is of paramount
foundational importance. The Axiom Schema of Separation (Zermelo's
*Aussonderungsaxiom*) is conservative: it can only carve out subsets of an
already existing set $A$. It can never leave the rank of $A$ or construct
sets of larger size.

The Axiom Schema of Replacement, introduced by Abraham Fraenkel and
Thoralf Skolem in 1922, is an expansive generative principle: if a
definable class operation associates each element of a set $A$ with a
uniquely determined set $y$, then the entire collection of outputs
$\{F(x) : x \in A\}$ forms a valid set. Replacement is indispensable for
transfinite recursion and ordinal arithmetic, guaranteeing that sequences
indexed by ordinals (such as $\aleph_\omega = \bigcup_{n < \omega}
\aleph_n$) cohere into genuine sets.
